text:
Maya: Quick UX snag on small screens: when the left rail collapses into the overlay, it slides in from the left and covers the first column of the routes table. Users can't reach the row action hamburger beneath it. Short vid: https://imgur.com/efgh5678.mp4
Ravi: repro'd on Pixel 4a chrome. Steps: pinch zoom out -> open sidebar -> try to tap row action. The overlay capture area is slightly wider than the visual rail (looks like z-index + padding issue).
Jordan: Might be related to our inert/focus trap logic for the overlay. We add a backdrop with pointer-events but the rail container has an extra 12px left margin that extends hit area.
Nina: design note: when the rail is overlay mode we should reduce its width to 72px (icon only) at <= 360px width, and the rest of nav can be expanded via a disclosure. That keeps table tappable. Also add visible focus ring on the active nav item.
Maya: agree on 72px collapsed, but on very narrow screens the table content becomes cramped. We should allow horizontal scrolling for the table body while keeping the header sticky and not letting the sidebar overlay hide primary actions.
Ravi: proposed CSS diff idea: .rail--overlay { right: auto; left: 0; width: 72px; transform: translateX(-100%); } .rail--overlay.open { transform: translateX(0); } and ensure .rail { pointer-events: auto; } backdrop { pointer-events: none; } This forces click-through area only on the visible rail.
Jordan: careful: pointer-events none on backdrop will break closing on tap outside. Better: backdrop captures taps but we clamp rail hitbox using overflow: hidden on rail-wrapper and set rail-inner { margin-left: 0; }
Nina: copy tweak: change "Open details" -> "Open route" in the mobile row action for context. Also change the empty state CTA from "Add route" to "Create a route" for consistency with onboarding flows.
Maya: accessibility: when the rail opens, focus should move to the first nav button and the previously focused table row should get aria-hidden="true" to avoid screen reader confusion. Add role="dialog" and aria-modal="true" for the overlay.
Ravi: QA-bot flagged an edge case: on foldables the table cell truncation breaks the copy measurement and multi-line rows jump when the rail toggles. Repro: Galaxy Fold in folded state. Screenshot: https://tests.redwood/failures/5621
Jordan: solution: use CSS contain: layout on row cells and set min-widths and `white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis;` for compact breakpoint <= 420px. For rows that need multiline we can show a stacked detail row toggled by the kebab menu.
Nina: small animation ask: when rail opens the table should slide left by exactly the rail width (72px) with a 160ms ease-out to make the relationship obvious. Avoid layout thrash by using transform: translateX on the table container.
QA-bot: added mobile regression tests under mobile/rail-overlay to CI. Failing runs: 3/5 on Safari iOS 15, 1/4 on Android Chrome. Ticket: RD-3498.
design-bot: new figma plate uploaded with 72px collapsed rail + overlay states: https://figma.com/file/ABC/compact-rail-mobile — includes specs for touch target, spacing, and header pinning. :memo:
Maya: will accept PR once it includes: 1) CSS clamp breakpoints for <= 360px and <= 420px, 2) focus management + aria attributes, 3) copy updates for row action + empty state, 4) visual tests and a short video in PR.
Ravi: starting a small PR now, will pair with Jordan on the foldable test harness later today.
Maya: tagging RD-3498 as P2 fix, aiming for next patch release. Thanks all.
